CRITICAL: these service categorys are ADMINISTRATIVE CONVENTIONS, not common-sense semantic classes. An organization often files an municipal service request under a service category that contradicts its literal wording (e.g. a request that mentions one topic is routed by the ACTION or WORKFLOW involved, not the topic named). Your job is to capture the organization's ACTUAL filing behavior as shown in the examples, even where it defies intuition. Never correct the organization; describe it.
Descriptions must be MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. If a phrase/feature appears under several service categorys, assign it to the MOST FREQUENT one and tell the others to exclude it.

Study the examples for CONVENTIONS that a common-sense classifier would get wrong: wording that suggests one service category but is actually filed under another. State those explicitly.

For EACH service category output one line: "<name>: <what this organization files here, including any counterintuitive cases> | NOT: <what looks like it belongs but is filed elsewhere>". Use the exact names. Output all 18 lines, nothing else.
response:
Blocked Street: Roll-off dumpsters placed on or along the street that obstruct travel or sit long-term, including behind a building if it sits in the street/right-of-way. | NOT: cars parked on lawns (Parking on Unimproved Surface); sign issues (Temporary Signage w/o permit); drainage/flooding (Sidewalk Snow Removal).

Excessive Growth: Tall grass/weeds and general yard maintenance neglect (front/back yards, businesses), including unmowed yards and piles of molded/mowed grass left on site. | NOT: visibility/line-of-sight complaints due to vegetation (Line of Sight); litter/trash accumulation complaints (Trash).

Line of Sight: Visibility obstructions at corners/intersections caused by vegetation or fences (e.g., bushes, overgrown vegetation, chain link fence with slats) that block the view. | NOT: general overgrowth/yard maintenance (Excessive Growth); driver behavior complaints like red-light running (Traffic Related Complaints).

Parking on Unimproved Surface: Vehicles parked on lawns/grass or other non-improved surfaces; attempts to create/expand gravel parking or re-grading to park; vehicles partly on grass and partly on street. | NOT: dumpsters blocking streets (Blocked Street); general on-street parking violations unrelated to surface (not covered here).

Parks & Playgrounds: Parks programming/amenities feedback (e.g., comments about summer concerts). | NOT: mowing/overgrowth in parks or grounds (Excessive Growth); signage issues (Temporary Signage w/o permit).

Recycling: Curbside recycling set-out violations—unsorted or improperly sorted recyclables, mixing recyclables with trash, items not accepted, and tag/sticker-based rejections. | NOT: yard waste set-out/sticker violations (Yard Waste); missed trash pickup or trash container problems (Trash).

Sewer Problems (Sanitary Sewers): Sanitary sewer issues—backups, toilets backing up, strong sewer odors, private sewer pump leaks causing flow in street; post-sewer-work yard restoration requests (stakes/posts removal, yard repair) filed here. | NOT: stormwater/drainage or street flooding (Sidewalk Snow Removal); water main/meter pit leaks or street buckling (Water Utility Problems).

Sidewalk & Curb Complaints: Used as a routing bucket for sanitation communications such as faxed/missed trash pickup with no notice left. | NOT: actual sidewalk/curb defects or snow issues (Street Snow Removal for sidewalk snow; Sidewalk Snow Removal for drainage).

Sidewalk Snow Removal: Stormwater drainage problems—flooded inlets/intersections, detention ponds full, water bubbling up from street, water standing in street, yards acting as storm drains. Counterintuitively, this is for drainage, not snow. | NOT: unshoveled/icy sidewalks (Street Snow Removal); sanitary sewer backups (Sewer Problems (Sanitary Sewers)).

Street Snow Removal: Sidewalk snow/ice not cleared—unshoveled sidewalks and walkways along streets and blocks. Counterintuitively, sidewalk snow is filed here. | NOT: drainage/flooding issues (Sidewalk Snow Removal); road plowing/ice control requests on the driving lanes (not shown here).

Temporary Signage w/o permit: Temporary banners/signs/sandwich boards and “now hiring” banners on properties/buildings, including off-premise banners. | NOT: permanent sign permits/violations (not here); parking or traffic signs (Traffic Related Complaints).

Traffic Related Complaints: General traffic behavior/safety complaints such as motorists running red lights. | NOT: visibility/line-of-sight due to vegetation or fences (Line of Sight); parking on grass or private property surface issues (Parking on Unimproved Surface).

Trash: Solid waste service issues—missed trash pickup, improper/overfull/unacceptable containers, missing required stickers/tags, courtesy pickups, and litter complaints (including litter in yards). | NOT: recycling sorting/mixing violations (Recycling); yard waste set-out/weight/sticker/missed collection (Yard Waste).

Unsafe Buildings: Vacant/abandoned or unsecured/dangerous structures (e.g., roof failing, unsecured trailer after fire). | NOT: overgrowth/yard neglect (Excessive Growth); trash accumulation (Trash).

Water Quality: Customer-side water service/quality and simple service requests—after-hours or routine turn-ons/turn-offs, minor “leak at meter” reports, in-home issues like water heater trouble or pipe rattling. | NOT: main breaks, street bubbling, meter pit damage, open holes (Water Utility Problems); billing/credits (Water Utility Billing Problems).

Water Utility Billing Problems: Billing/credit/account disputes and adjustments (e.g., requests for partial credit, questionable bill amounts). | NOT: service activation/shutoffs or field valve operations (Water Utility Problems or Water Quality as above); leaks or water quality/noise (Water Utility Problems/Water Quality).

Water Utility Problems: Distribution system/field-crew issues—water bubbling up in street, leaks causing street buckling, open holes near curb/sidewalk, meter pit leaks/damage (e.g., from car accidents), and delinquency-related or after-hours field shutoff/turn-on operations. | NOT: customer-side quality/noise/water heater or simple turn-on requests (Water Quality); billing disputes (Water Utility Billing Problems).

Yard Waste: Yard waste collection issues—missing/incorrect stickers, overweight/over 40 lb set-outs, and missed yard waste pickup. | NOT: recycling sorting/mixing (Recycling); regular trash service issues or litter (Trash).

{"dimension":"Waste stream/material handled (general refuse vs yard organics), not the type of violation (sticker/weight/missed pickup)","gt_signal":"Generic bags/cans without any 'yard' mention; refuse-specific cues like 35‑gallon can limits, trash/garbage/refuse terms, and citation code 944; courtesy pickup/litter context","pr_signal":"Explicit yard-waste markers: the words 'yard waste/yardwaste', leaves/brush/bundles, yard program limits (40‑lb, 32‑gal yard can), and citation code 950; phrases like 'missed pick‑up/yard waste'","culprit":"The Yard Waste rule fires on generic 'sticker/overweight/missed pickup' language, while Trash’s neg rule excludes those topics, so keywords like 'sticker' and 'weight' pushed non‑yard items to Yard Waste","fix":"Only classify as Yard Waste when there is an explicit yard‑waste indicator (e.g., 'yard waste/yardwaste', brush/leaves, 32‑gal/40‑lb, code 950); otherwise treat generic sticker/weight/bag violations (incl. 35‑gal, code 944) as Trash."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/context of the problem: on‑property blight/code‑enforcement vs curbside solid‑waste service/set‑out compliance","gt_signal":"Accumulated debris/trash on private property or grounds (side/back yard, on the lot, business premises, recurring accumulation, overflowing private dumpsters) with no can/size/pickup/sticker service cues","pr_signal":"Municipal collection/service cues: cans/containers, 35‑gal limits, missed/courtesy pickup, set‑out at curb with required stickers/tags, container acceptability","culprit":"'Trash' positive rule’s broad “litter complaint” (and sticker/tag keywords) grabs anything mentioning trash, while 'Excessive Growth' positive rule omits trash/junk accumulation on private property","fix":"Treat trash/junk accumulation on private property/grounds (including overflowing private dumpsters) as Excessive Growth, reserving Trash for curbside collection/service and container/sticker/pickup issues only."}

{"dimension":"Issue nature/responsibility: operational service performance (pickup missed/handled) vs resident set-out compliance (sorting/eligibility)","gt_signal":"References to missed pickup, courtesy drops/picks, crew actions or schedule/delay—i.e., a service execution problem the hauler must resolve, even when it’s recycling","pr_signal":"Language about recyclables being unsorted/mixed/not accepted, DO NOT MIX, must be sorted, tag/sticker rejection—i.e., a resident sorting/set-out violation with no collection performed","culprit":"The Recycling positive trigger on “unsorted/not properly sorted” (and Trash’s blanket negation of recycling sorting/mixing) overrides missed‑pickup and courtesy‑pickup cases that should be Trash","fix":"Classify by problem type: route recycling missed‑pickup and courtesy‑pickup/education cases to Trash, reserving Recycling for pure set‑out/sorting violations where no collection occurs"}

{"dimension":"the serviced waste stream/program (yard waste vs regular trash), not the type of violation or action taken","gt_signal":"context that ties the issue to the yard‑waste program—seasonality (e.g., no winter collection), organics packaging rules (yard waste not allowed in plastic bags; paper yard bags/bundles), and size/weight/sticker violations framed for yard waste (35‑gal/40‑lb yard‑waste limits)","pr_signal":"generic solid‑waste cues—trash/garbage can issues (can size >35 gal), courtesy pickups, and sticker/tag problems stated without any organics/seasonal context, plus litter/missed trash","culprit":"Trash POS rule “improper/overfull/unacceptable containers, missing stickers/tags, courtesy pickups” is overbroad and captures size/‘improper container’/‘courtesy pickup’ cases that lack explicit trash wording","fix":"Disambiguate by waste stream: only treat size/weight/sticker/courtesy violations as Trash when explicitly tied to trash/garbage cans, and route them to Yard Waste when paired with yard‑waste context such as no winter collection or plastic‑bag-not-allowed packaging rules."}

{"dimension":"Actionable solid-waste service request vs administrative routing/hand-off note","gt_signal":"States a concrete service need (missed collection/please pick up) for a waste stream without the 'no notice left' routing qualifier—intent is to get collection done","pr_signal":"Reads like a routing memo rather than a service request—explicitly flags 'no notice left' or similar internal hand-off language (often 'to sanitation')","culprit":"The keyword 'faxed' (and/or 'faxed' + 'missed pick-up') being treated as sufficient for Sidewalk & Curb without requiring the 'no notice left' condition","fix":"Only route to Sidewalk & Curb when a faxed sanitation note includes the 'no notice left' cue; otherwise treat missed pickups as the appropriate solid-waste service request."}

{"dimension":"Intent and locus of the vegetation problem: traffic-safety sightlines at public street intersections vs property/yard overgrowth (including driveway/frontage) maintenance","gt_signal":"Framed as yard/ROW maintenance on or in front of a specific property (neighbor’s, address, over a wall) or blocking a private driveway/egress; mentions grass/weeds/bushes encroaching without anchoring it to a public intersection sight triangle","pr_signal":"Ties vegetation/fence specifically to an intersection/corner and a visibility hazard for roadway users (e.g., “NW corner,” “can’t see traffic,” “allow traffic to be seen”)","culprit":"The Line of Sight positive rule that keys on “visibility obstructions at corners/intersections” (and keywords like corner/intersection/see) without excluding private driveways/frontage","fix":"Limit Line of Sight to public street-intersection sight‑triangle obstructions; route driveway/frontage visibility or general yard/ROW overgrowth—even if it affects seeing when pulling out—to Excessive Growth."}

{"dimension":"material stream being serviced (recycling program vs trash program), independent of issue type (missed pickup, container size, courtesy, etc.)","gt_signal":"the text ties the issue to the recycling stream—explicit mentions of recycling, sorting/contamination instructions (e.g., remove trash from recyclables), recycle cart/bin/blue cart, or a pickup/reject/courtesy explicitly for recycling","pr_signal":"the issue is framed as trash service—trash cans/bags, stickered trash rules, generic missed pickup or courtesy pickup with no recycling marker, container-size limits with no recycle indicator, or the bare word “trash” not explicitly in a recycling-contamination context","culprit":"Trash positive rule matching generic service-type cues (missed pick-up, courtesy pick up, unacceptable/oversize container) and the keyword “trash,” without first checking which stream is involved","fix":"Route by stream first: if the text indicates recycling or contamination/sorting of recyclables, send to Recycling even when it mentions missed pickup, courtesy pickup, container size, or the word “trash.”"}

{"dimension":"Living vegetation condition (growth/maintenance) vs accumulation/dumping of refuse (discarded materials, including cut vegetation)","gt_signal":"Complaint centers on removal of discarded materials—junk/construction debris or cut vegetation (brush/trees/limbs) left or dumped as piles, often in the street—with no mention of mowing, height, or living plant growth.","pr_signal":"Mentions unmowed/tall grass/weeds or overall yard maintenance neglect, or explicitly a pile of mowed/molded grass left on the property.","culprit":"Excessive Growth positive rule for “general yard maintenance neglect… including… piles of molded/mowed grass left on site,” combined with vegetation words like brush/trees and “piled,” is over-broad and pulled in junk/brush piles.","fix":"Restrict Excessive Growth to living vegetation (tall grass/weeds) and mowed-grass piles, and classify any accumulation of cut vegetation (brush/limbs/logs), construction debris, or junk—especially when piled or in the street—as Trash."}

{"dimension":"Primary subject of the complaint: yard/property condition/maintenance vs parking behavior/use of surface","gt_signal":"The complaint targets the state of the yard (neglect, junk/trash under a tarp, debris on the lawn) as the core issue; any vehicle mention is incidental or one of multiple issues framed as general property maintenance","pr_signal":"The vehicle and where it is placed are the focus—explicitly parked on grass/lawn/unimproved surface or creating/expanding gravel for parking—without broader yard-neglect context","culprit":"The PR positive rule keyed to 'vehicles parked on lawns/grass' (and even 'parks his vehicle') fires on any park+grass/driveway phrasing, while EG’s positives are too narrowly tied to 'tall grass/weeds' and miss junk/tarp/trash yard-neglect reports","fix":"When a report mixes parking with yard-neglect (junk/trash/tarp/overgrowth), treat it as Excessive Growth and reserve Parking on Unimproved Surface for complaints whose primary issue is vehicles on grass/unimproved surfaces or surface modifications, not driveway blockage or general yard condition."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/operational locus: utility-side field infrastructure work vs customer-side quality/account service requests","gt_signal":"Mentions of utility infrastructure or field intervention—meter pit/curb stop, street/curb/yard damage, external impact (e.g., car accident), or a requested shut‑off that requires operating utility hardware","pr_signal":"Routine customer intents on the customer side—after‑hours service activation, generic “leak at meter” with no pit/damage context, and in‑home issues like water heaters","culprit":"Water Quality positive rule for “after-hours turn‑ons/turn‑offs” and “minor ‘leak at meter’ reports,” with the keywords AFTER HOURS, TURNED OFF, and LEAK AT METER overriding ‘meter pit’/accident context","fix":"Reserve Water Quality for customer-side quality/admin requests (e.g., turn-ons, generic meter leaks), and route any case involving the meter pit/curb stop, external damage, or field shut‑offs/repairs to Water Utility Problems—even if phrased as a simple after‑hours request."}

{"dimension":"Service context and responsibility: curbside collection compliance vs on‑premises property blight/neglect","gt_signal":"Trash/junk anchored to a specific property’s grounds or structures (side of house, around a shed/garage, business grounds, overflowing private dumpster), with accumulation/overflow/“again” framing and no can‑size/limit/pickup compliance focus—even if the word “trash” is used.","pr_signal":"Explicit solid‑waste service cues about curbside set‑out and compliance (stickers/tags required, 35‑gal can/limits, courtesy/missed pickup), often in terse directive phrasing like “Bags must have sticker attached.”","culprit":"Keywording on “trash,” “dumpster,” and “curb/stickers” without checking whether the complaint is about collection compliance vs property blight; the Trash rule’s broad “litter complaint/overfull container” language pulled in private‑property dumpster overflow and yard junk.","fix":"Treat trash/junk on private property (yards, around structures, overflowing private dumpsters) as Excessive Growth, and reserve Trash for curbside collection/set‑out compliance issues signaled by stickers/tags, can size/limits, or pickup status."}

{"dimension":"Remedy/intent: discrete trash/debris removal by sanitation versus property-maintenance of living vegetation or chronic yard blight","gt_signal":"Complaint centers on removable refuse or dumped items (loose bags, shopping carts, cut limbs/trees) or pickup/service cues—the action needed is cleanup/haul-away, not mowing","pr_signal":"Complaint describes a neglected property condition (tall grass/weeds/hedges, unmowed, or a persistently junk-strewn yard) without pickup/service cues—the action needed is owner maintenance/compliance","culprit":"Excessive Growth POS rule: \"Accumulated household trash or junk blighting private yards/lots...\"","fix":"Direct reports about discrete trash/debris (bags, carts, cut brush/trees) to Trash even on private yards; reserve Excessive Growth for living vegetation overgrowth or diffuse, ongoing yard blight lacking a specific trash-removal cue"}

{"dimension":"Intent + site context: public intersection sight‑triangle safety vs a specific property’s frontage/driveway and yard‑maintenance overgrowth","gt_signal":"Anchored to a single address or a driveway/frontage (e.g., “pulling out,” “in front of [address]”), with yard‑neglect framing (grass/weeds/bushes growing out over a wall/sidewalk/drive), i.e., a property‑maintenance overgrowth causing nuisance or driveway egress visibility","pr_signal":"Framed as an intersection/corner hazard for cross‑traffic: mentions cross‑streets, “NW/NE corner,” or traffic visibility (“allow traffic to be seen,” “can’t see at the intersection”) without anchoring to one property/driveway","culprit":"The Line of Sight positive rule that fires on any “intersection/corner” + visibility language; keywords like “intersection,” “corner,” and “can’t see” overrode the property/driveway and yard‑neglect context","fix":"Use Line of Sight only for public intersection/crosswalk sight‑triangle visibility (often signaled by cross‑streets or corner orientation); if the complaint ties overgrowth to a specific address or driveway/frontage—even if visibility is affected—treat it as Excessive Growth."}

{"dimension":"Waste-stream context: recycling-program compliance/blue-cart use vs generic trash service/container issues","gt_signal":"Clear tie to the recycling stream or intent to enforce recycling rules: explicit 'recycling' mention, blue cart/bin or code 945, sorting/contamination directives (e.g., 'Please sort & remove trash'), courtesy/education after write-ups, or recycle-can sizing/eligibility","pr_signal":"Stream-agnostic trash-service cues: 'missed pick-up' without recycling context, generic container-size/limit phrases ('can too big', 'exceeds 35 gal'), sticker/tag language, or bare 'courtesy pickup'","culprit":"Over-broad Trash POS for 'courtesy pickups' and container size, plus the Recycling NEG that sends 'missed recycling pickup' to Trash","fix":"Anchor classification to the stream: if context indicates the recycling program (recycling mention/code, sorting/contamination directives, courtesy/education, or blue-cart/can sizing), keep it in Recycling; reserve Trash for trash-stream containers/stickers and missed trash pickup only."}

{"dimension":"Program context and issue type: yard‑waste program compliance/policy vs general collection operations (missed pickup/limits/bulky) regardless of material","gt_signal":"Operational service failure or generic limits without explicit yard‑waste‑program cues (missed pickup, overweight/container size with no yard‑waste stickers/bags/codes) or ‘other/bulky’ items like a Christmas tree","pr_signal":"Explicit yard‑waste program context and compliance: yard‑waste terms tied to stickers/yard bags/citation code 950/seasonality or clear yard‑waste set‑out violations","culprit":"Overbroad Yard Waste positives—“Missed … yard‑waste collection” and “size/weight/container limits exceeded” firing without program cues, plus treating material words (e.g., “tree”) as yard‑waste","fix":"Require explicit yard‑waste program context (stickers/yard bags/code 950/seasonality) for Yard Waste, and default missed pickups, generic weight/container violations, and ‘other’ items like Xmas trees to Trash unless tied to the yard‑waste program."}

{"dimension":"Primary violation focus: property maintenance/blight (vegetation/junk) vs parking-surface misuse (vehicle on non‑improved surface)","gt_signal":"The report centers on the condition of the property—overgrowth or junk/trash accumulation (e.g., junk under tarp, trash on lawn)—with any vehicle mention being incidental or about obstruction/blocking rather than the surface it’s parked on.","pr_signal":"The report’s focus is a vehicle located on a prohibited surface (grass/dirt) or creation/expansion of a gravel parking area (e.g., “parked on the lawn/grass,” “re‑graveled/gravel parking area”).","culprit":"Over-broad match to the Parking rule “Vehicles parked on lawns/grass…” triggered by phrases like “cars parked on the lawn” and “parks his vehicle,” without checking issue primacy or surface relevance.","fix":"Only classify as Parking on Unimproved Surface when the primary concern is a vehicle on grass/dirt or creating an unimproved parking area; if yard trash/overgrowth is also reported or the parking is about blocking/access (not surface), treat it as Excessive Growth."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/operational locus: utility-side field infrastructure work vs customer-side quality/account service requests","gt_signal":"Mentions of utility infrastructure or field intervention—meter pit/curb stop, street/curb/yard damage, external impact (e.g., car accident), or a requested shut‑off that requires operating utility hardware","pr_signal":"Routine customer intents on the customer side—after‑hours service activation, generic “leak at meter” with no pit/damage context, and in‑home issues like water heaters","culprit":"Water Quality positive rule for “after-hours turn‑ons/turn‑offs” and “minor ‘leak at meter’ reports,” with the keywords AFTER HOURS, TURNED OFF, and LEAK AT METER overriding ‘meter pit’/accident context","fix":"Reserve Water Quality for customer-side quality/admin requests (e.g., turn-ons, generic meter leaks), and route any case involving the meter pit/curb stop, external damage, or field shut‑offs/repairs to Water Utility Problems—even if phrased as a simple after‑hours request."}

{"dimension":"service intent: compliance/education notice vs operational collection action","gt_signal":"mentions an actual or requested collection action (picked/collected, courtesy drop/pickup, crew went out) or pickup service outcome, even when tied to recycling noncompliance","pr_signal":"only documents recycling noncompliance and gives warnings/directions (unsorted, do not mix, must be sorted) with no pickup action performed or requested","culprit":"Recycling positive rule #4 (courtesy actions tied to recycling compliance) pulls in cases where a courtesy pickup/collection actually occurred","fix":"Clarify that any case involving actual or requested collection (including courtesy drops/pickups) goes to Trash; Recycling is reserved for compliance warnings/directions without collection action."}

{"dimension":"service-program transaction vs property/area blight condition (who/what context is responsible)","gt_signal":"describes trash/junk as an accumulating or overflowing condition on/around a specific property, alley, or private dumpster (side of house, on grounds, causing rats, recurring), without framing it as a collection-program action/compliance request; any mention of stickers/tags is incidental, not an instruction","pr_signal":"frames the issue in collection-program terms—can/cart size limits, tags/stickers as a requirement, missed pickup, or prescriptive notes like “must have sticker” tied to curbside set-out/compliance","culprit":"Excessive Growth neg rule that forces any mention of tags/stickers or 'at curb' into Trash, plus over-weighting of 'sticker/tag' keywords","fix":"Only route to Trash when the text clearly invokes the curbside collection program (can/cart, missed pickup, or prescriptive sticker/size compliance); treat location-based accumulation/overflow on property, alleys, or dumpsters as Excessive Growth even if words like 'trash,' 'untagged,' or 'at curb' appear."}

{"dimension":"Intent/action: sanitation removal of discrete non-living debris vs property maintenance/vegetation overgrowth/overall blight","gt_signal":"Describes removable refuse or objects to be hauled away—loose trash/litter, junk piles, cut trees/brush, or even junk-filled/’junk’ vehicles—often spreading or overflowing, with no mowing/overgrowth ask; reads like a cleanup/pickup request","pr_signal":"Centers on living vegetation or ongoing yard neglect—unmowed grass, weeds, hedge/clipping issues—or a vague “yard is a mess/needs maintenance” condition without naming specific removable items","culprit":"Excessive Growth POS rule allowing “accumulated trash/junk blighting a property…with no curbside context,” combined with keyword bias for “yard/grass,” and no exception for vehicles/cut trees","fix":"Restrict Excessive Growth’s “accumulated trash/junk” to generalized hoarding/maintenance conditions, and send any report that names specific removable debris (including cut trees/brush, loose litter, junk vehicles or vehicles filled with junk) to Trash even if on a yard."}

{"dimension":"location and responsibility: public intersection sight-triangle safety vs private-property frontage/driveway maintenance/encroachment","gt_signal":"the obstruction is tied to a specific property’s frontage/driveway/sidewalk or vegetation growing over a wall/fence—often phrased as “pulling out” without naming a street-street corner—i.e., a yard-maintenance/encroachment issue at an address","pr_signal":"explicit intersection/corner framing (e.g., “at X & Y,” “NW corner”) with visibility-for-traffic language (can’t see cars/pedestrians, allow traffic to be seen) indicating a sight-triangle hazard","culprit":"an over-broad keyword trigger mapping any “can’t see/pulling out” or any mention of “intersection” to Line of Sight, overriding frontage/driveway and specific-address context","fix":"Only use Line of Sight when the report clearly targets a public street-street corner sight triangle; treat visibility loss tied to a specific property’s frontage/driveway or general overgrowth/encroachment as Excessive Growth."}

{"dimension":"Which waste stream/program the note is about (recycling-compliance/blue-cart program vs general trash/sticker rules), not whether a pickup is mentioned","gt_signal":"Explicit recycling context or program markers: the word recycling, blue cart/bin, code 945, instructions to sort/remove trash from recycling, or write-up/education about recycling—even if it also mentions a pickup/courtesy pickup","pr_signal":"Generic trash service cues with no recycling markers: can/bag size limits (35 gal), sticker/tag requirements (e.g., 944), courtesy pickups framed as solid-waste service, or bare words like trash without a recycling-context phrase","culprit":"Recycling.neg rule that forces any pickup/route/schedule mention (including missed recycling pickup) into Trash, plus over-weighting of generic size/sticker and the word “trash” over code 945 and sorting context","fix":"Prioritize the stream/program: anything explicitly tied to the recycling program (recycling/blue cart/code 945/sort-contamination) stays Recycling even if pickup or the word “trash” is mentioned; reserve Trash for trash-stream size/sticker issues lacking recycling markers."}

{"dimension":"Issue intent: operational service failure/collection request vs program/compliance information about yard-waste rules","gt_signal":"It reports a missed pickup or asks for collection (e.g., “missed Wednesday/last week,” “make sure it’s collected,” courtesy/call-in), with no citation/sticker/rule language—even if the material mentioned is yard waste or a Christmas tree","pr_signal":"It focuses on yard-waste program attributes—stickers/tags/fees/codes, set-out/packaging/size/container rules, or seasonal suspension—i.e., citations or guidance, not a pickup request","culprit":"Yard Waste positive rule: “Missed, delayed, or seasonally suspended yard-waste collection,” which over-absorbs missed-collection complaints","fix":"Treat any missed-collection or collection-request item as Trash regardless of material; reserve Yard Waste for citations/compliance/seasonality or program rules only."}

{"dimension":"Primary nuisance focus: property-grounds blight/maintenance (vegetation or junk) vs vehicle placement on a non‑improved surface","gt_signal":"Text centers on yard neglect or blight at a specific property (overgrown vegetation or accumulated trash/junk on the grounds) with no curbside service cues; any vehicle mention is incidental or secondary.","pr_signal":"Text centers on vehicles being on grass/dirt or creating/expanding a non‑improved/gravel parking area; the issue is where the vehicle sits, not general yard condition or driveway obstruction.","culprit":"Over-broad reliance on 'park/vehicle/lawn' keywords routed items to Parking on Unimproved Surface without requiring an explicit non‑improved surface focus and without downweighting mixed reports that include trash/junk.","fix":"Only use Parking on Unimproved Surface when the main complaint is vehicles on grass/dirt or creating gravel parking; if junk/yard blight is also present or primary, keep it in Excessive Growth even if vehicles are mentioned."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/operational locus: utility-side field infrastructure work vs customer-side quality/account service requests","gt_signal":"Mentions of utility infrastructure or field intervention—meter pit/curb stop, street/curb/yard damage, external impact (e.g., car accident), or a requested shut‑off that requires operating utility hardware","pr_signal":"Routine customer intents on the customer side—after‑hours service activation, generic “leak at meter” with no pit/damage context, and in‑home issues like water heaters","culprit":"Water Quality positive rule for “after-hours turn‑ons/turn‑offs” and “minor ‘leak at meter’ reports,” with the keywords AFTER HOURS, TURNED OFF, and LEAK AT METER overriding ‘meter pit’/accident context","fix":"Reserve Water Quality for customer-side quality/admin requests (e.g., turn-ons, generic meter leaks), and route any case involving the meter pit/curb stop, external damage, or field shut‑offs/repairs to Water Utility Problems—even if phrased as a simple after‑hours request."}

{"dimension":"Type of interaction: operational collection service vs compliance/education-only notice","gt_signal":"Mentions a collection action or need (missed/not picked, was picked, courtesy drop/pickup, crew went out/route) indicating field service occurred or is required","pr_signal":"Pure recycling compliance language (unsorted/contaminated, DO NOT MIX, notices/tags/citations/instructions) with no pickup or crew action","culprit":"Recycling.pos[0]/pos[1] fired on 'unsorted recycle' and 'notice' while the negation missed pickup synonyms like 'courtesy drops' and 'picked'","fix":"Override Recycling whenever any pickup/crew action is mentioned (missed/picked/courtesy drop/went out), reserving Recycling for compliance-only notes with no collection service."}

{"pos":["Citation or tag explicitly for yard waste, including code 950 or wording like yard-waste tag or sticker.","Mentions required yard-waste sticker or wrong/absent sticker, with explicit yard-waste terms.","Preparation violations for yard materials: plastic bags, unbundled brush, oversize/untied bundles, or over the 40‑lb yard-waste limit.","Container/can/cart issues tied to yard-waste program (yard-waste can size, approved paper yard bags), explicitly naming yard waste or yard bags.","Seasonal or program notices about yard-waste service (e.g., winter suspension, holiday schedule, accepted materials/rules), not a specific collection request."],"remap":["if citation code 944 appears, classify as Trash instead","if only a 35‑gallon container limit is cited without any yard‑waste terms, classify as Trash instead","if overweight/too heavy or sticker/tag requirement appears without yard‑waste/organics cues, classify as Trash instead","if it reports a missed pickup or requests collection for yard waste or Christmas tree, classify as Trash instead"]}

{"pos":["Overgrown vegetation from a specific private property: tall grass/weeds/hedges/vines encroaching or obstructing its yard, sidewalk, wall/fence, mailbox, frontage, or driveway.","Persistent yard or lot maintenance neglect at a residence or business: unmowed lawn, unmaintained landscaping, recurring overgrowth or encroachment complaints.","Visibility loss while exiting a driveway or along a property's frontage caused by that property's vegetation; no public street-street intersection sight triangle referenced.","Generalized accumulation of trash/junk blighting a property's grounds, adjacent alley, or private dumpster overflow, without collection-program cues; 'at curb' may be incidental.","Large piles or windrows of mowed grass clippings left on the yard; excludes discrete cut limbs or trees."],"remap":["if visibility obstruction names a public street-street corner, crosswalk, or intersection sight triangle, classify as Line of Sight instead","if the main complaint is vehicles parked/stored on grass/dirt or creating unimproved parking, not junk/abandoned removal, classify as Parking on Unimproved Surface instead","if the request seeks sanitation pickup or references carts/cans, missed or scheduled pickup, bulk pickup, or cart-size limits, classify as Trash instead","if it names specific removable debris—loose bags/litter, furniture/appliances, tires, shopping carts, cut trees/brush, or junk/abandoned vehicles—without overgrowth context, classify as Trash instead"]}

{"pos":["Recycling compliance: unsorted/contaminated recyclables, non-accepted items, or trash in recycling; includes tags/citations, education, code 945, or blue cart/bin mentions.","Instructions to correct recycling set-out: sort/separate, remove trash from recycling, or place blue cart at specified location; no collection requested.","Program-specific recycling container issues: eligibility, authorized use, size/too-big, or overflow for blue cart/bin; excludes route, schedule, or crew performance.","Education-only follow-ups after recycling write-ups: document warnings/outreach or compliance notes; no pickup/drop action.","Any request explicitly about recycling/blue cart/code 945 compliance remains here even if 'trash' or 'missed pickup' words appear."],"remap":["if it states a collection occurred (picked up/collected/emptied or courtesy drop/delivery completed), classify as Trash instead","if the container issue is about a trash/garbage cart rather than a recycling blue cart/bin, classify as Trash instead","if it concerns yard waste/compost/leaves or their set-out/stickers, classify as Yard Waste instead","if size/sticker/overflow compliance is about general trash rules and lacks recycling/blue cart/code 945 markers, classify as Trash instead"]}

{"pos":["Vehicles parked with any wheels on grass, dirt, mud, or other unpaved ground of a private lot, including front, side, or rear yards.","Creating or expanding gravel or loose-surface areas to serve as parking on yards or setbacks, even if no vehicle is present.","Vehicles parked on landscaping areas not designed as driveways or permitted pads, such as mulch beds, landscaped rock, or vegetated tree lawns/hellstrips."],"remap":["if overgrown vegetation, tall weeds, or \"excessive growth\" is reported alongside vehicles on lawn/yard, classify as Excessive Growth instead.","if junk, trash, debris, or tarp-covered items on the property are cited along with cars on the lawn, classify as Excessive Growth instead."]}

{"pos":["Visible water emerging from ground/road/curb/sidewalk or pavement buckling/voids indicating a main or service-line leak in the public right‑of‑way.","Open hole, trench, depression, or unsafe condition at curb/sidewalk/right‑of‑way tied to water utility excavation, meter pit, curb box, or prior repair.","Meter pit or curb stop problems: leaking, flooded, damaged lid/box, stuck/broken valve, or vehicle impact damage requiring utility field response.","Utility field operations requested: shut‑off/turn‑on at curb stop or meter by utility staff, including delinquency, seasonal/vacancy, or after‑hours service.","Hydrant, valve box, or distribution hardware leaking, broken, or struck, requiring crew dispatch and repair in the distribution system."],"remap":["if complaint concerns taste, odor, discoloration, cloudy water, or air/noise in indoor plumbing or water heater, classify as Water Quality instead.","if request is routine move‑in/move‑out account turn‑on/off during business hours, with no curb stop or meter pit mentioned, classify as Water Quality instead.","if complaint is 'leak at meter' or leak after the meter on customer plumbing, not the meter pit/curb stop, classify as Water Quality instead.","if message is a billing/payment dispute or payment arrangement only, with no field work requested, classify as Water Utility Billing instead."]}

{"pos":["Requests to start/stop service or turn water on/off as a scheduling/account action, without meter pit/curb stop/street damage/emergency wording.","In-home water quality complaints—taste, odor, color, cloudy, sediment—or interior pressure/flow or plumbing noises, with no external infrastructure or street/yard terms.","Reports of minor leak at meter or within residence when location is private-side/unspecified; no 'meter pit', 'curb stop', street, yard, or damage context.","Customer issues/questions about property-owned water fixtures or appliances (e.g., water heater) affecting service/quality; excludes utility-owned equipment and billing.","After-hours routine service requests for activation, inspection, or customer-side assistance, explicitly non-emergency and lacking infrastructure damage keywords."],"remap":["if text mentions 'meter pit', 'curb stop', street valve, main break, street bubbling, or road/yard damage, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if requested shut-off references after-hours service charge, emergency, leak mitigation, or crew/valve operation, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if report cites external impact like car accident/vehicle strike causing leak or damage, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if billing, credits, payments, deposits, rates, or account balance are the focus, classify as Water Utility Bill instead"]}
